taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Andropogon gerardi Vitman. The widespread North American spelling Andropogon gerardii is retained as a primary alias/search term because it remains standard in many Texas and U.S. references.
look_here_first: BIG BLUESTEM: look for 2–6 exposed spikelet-bearing racemes arising close together at the top, often a three-toed turkey-foot. Trace the entire head; do not rely on color or count alone.

best_field_traits: Tall warm-season perennial with robust upright stems from a persistent crown or short rhizomes.
Typically 2–6 relatively stout exposed racemes radiating near the culm tip; commonly three suggest a turkey-foot.
Leaf blades commonly broader than little bluestem; collar often hairy, with a short chiefly membranous ligule.
Paired sessile/pedicelled spikelets along racemes, with awns; inspect with a lens for confirmation.
Not the many SHORT separately sheathed racemes of little bluestem or the brushy plume of bushy bluestem.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Follow branching, not autumn color. BIG: a few fairly stout, exposed racemes radiate near one culm tip. LITTLE: many short, silky racemes distributed on separate upper leafy branches. KR: multiple finer slender racemes in a clustered head can resemble BIG; count alone is not proof, so inspect attachment, leaf collar and mature spikelets. INDIANGRASS: one plume-like panicle rather than a true turkey-foot.
morphology_keys.photo_specific_evidence: The existing file 01-whole-plant.jpg is actually a leaf-collar/ligule macro; files 02 and 03 show multiple grasses and general habitat, not species-isolated diagnostic seedheads. Source descriptions and original thumbnails were inspected 2026-10-21. Do not use those three image filenames as evidence of the old roles.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Big bluestem: usually 2–6 exposed relatively stout racemes close together at the terminal head (often a turkey-foot). Little bluestem: many short silky racemes repeated on separate leafy upper branchlets. KR bluestem: long thin clustered terminal racemes, often overlapping in count, so use several characters rather than seedhead count alone. Bushy bluestem: bulky fuzzy plume. Broomsedge: narrower silky flowering units subtended by spathe-like sheaths. Indiangrass: elongated single plume-like inflorescence.

field_id_finish_pass.crew_memory_rule: BIG = a few STOUT exposed fingers near one top; LITTLE = many SHORT fuzzy racemes on different upper leafy branches.
field_id_finish_pass.look_here_first: Follow a complete flowering stem to the top. Look for several stout spikes projecting from near one point; photograph their common branching center before counting fingers.
field_sequence: Photograph a rooted mature culm from crown to upper seedhead, including the actual head branching point.
Count and TRACE exposed racemes: big bluestem often has 2–6 near the tip, usually thicker than KR, but their ranges overlap.
Inspect the same plant's leaf collar. A short chiefly membranous ligule and hairs around the collar support big bluestem; the approved Lavin image shows the ligule well.
Use a hand lens on attached sessile and pedicelled spikelets and awns; compare with verified KR bluestem, little bluestem, and Indiangrass.
If only a mixed-species prairie photo or vegetative shoot is available, record Andropogoneae / bluestem sp. rather than forcing a species.
important_cautions: Three-tipped turkey-foot is common but not mandatory: two to six exposed racemes can be present.
The old three-photo gallery was incorrectly labelled. Its existing whole-plant file is a collar macro; its other two files contain mixed grasses.
The external two macro views are from Montana, not Hays County; original labels and licenses are preserved.
No arrow is placed on a doubtful grass in the mixed-species photos.
Do not change the already reviewed Hays County native-range status from this photography audit.

lookalike_quick_key.cue: Short hairy racemes distributed through multiple upper leafy branches, not a few long exposed terminal fingers.
Introduced KR: typically several longer thinner fingerlike racemes gathered at the head; inspect collars/spikelets because count and outline overlap.
Bushy bluestem: dense brushy plume of crowded silky racemes instead of open turkey-foot branches.
Broomsedge: slender silky racemes associated with conspicuous spathe-like sheaths; not broad open fingers.
Indiangrass: solitary elongated plumelike panicle; not a digitate set of several fingers.
